entity.trigger_condition: Black tea is drunk with, or within 60 minutes of, a meal containing non-haem iron.
entity.population_description: Healthy adults eating a meal containing non-haem iron
entity.recommendation_text_template: Black tea with this meal can cut the non-haem iron you absorb by about {reduction_pct}%. Having it at least an hour after eating reduces this effect.
entity.applicability_notes: Overrides the generic polyphenol beverage rule for black tea. 60-minute window from Ahmad Fuzi 2017 (tea 1 h after the meal still inhibited about 18% vs 37% with the meal, so the effect is reduced, not removed). Adding milk does not remove the effect (Hurrell 1999).

evidence.inclusion_reason: Direct human radio-iron absorption evidence for polyphenol-containing beverages served with a meal.
evidence.synthesis_notes: Supports flagging black tea with a meal as a conflict.

paper.authors: Hurrell RF, Reddy M, Cook JD
paper.title: Inhibition of non-haem iron absorption in man by polyphenolic-containing beverages
paper.notes: Source of ABS_MOD_IRON_002 to 004. Calibration data: not used as held-out validation.

evidence.inclusion_reason: Stable-isotope crossover trial in healthy UK women (n=12) comparing tea with a meal and tea 1 h after.
evidence.synthesis_notes: Absorption 5.7% (water), 3.6% (tea with meal), 5.7% (tea 1 h after). Inhibition 37.2% vs 18.1%. Sets the 60-minute window only; absorption values are held out for validation.

paper.authors: Ahmad Fuzi SF, Koller D, Bruggraber S, Pereira DIA, Dainty JR, Mushtaq S
paper.title: A 1-h time interval between a meal containing iron and consumption of tea attenuates the inhibitory effects on iron absorption: a controlled trial in a cohort of healthy UK women using a stable iron isotope
paper.notes: Sets the 60-minute window for RULE_IRON_002/003. Absorption values held out for validation. Pages to verify.
